decisions.approvalNote: The user explicitly approved the revised intent-driven retained lifecycle, including install-and-activate, stopped-state uninstall, automatic visual launch on Start, server-only Start behavior, and Stop as the only running-state action.
decisions.context: Publish consolidation is user-directed. The lifecycle must preserve exact-release integrity, workspace isolation, truthful retained state, audit history, and secure runtime authority while presenting only actions that are valid for the current system state.

consequences: Not installed exposes Install; Install performs install then activation without exposing a separate initial Activate step
Installed, active, and stopped exposes Start, Deactivate, and Uninstall; installed, inactive, and stopped exposes Activate and Uninstall
Running exposes Stop only; Stop returns the system to its prior installed activation state and eligible stopped controls
Uninstall is available for any stopped installed system and records an auditable retained transition instead of deleting history
Opaque deployment and run identifiers remain internal, duplicate install intents are idempotent, and the standalone Run & Test tab is removed

Qualified built-in visual systems open automatically from verified exact-release declarative content and typed runtime bindings; nonvisual servers start without an Open control; imported or authored execution remains unavailable without a qualified sandbox
options.label: Intent-driven retained lifecycle
options.summary: Retain one application-owned current deployment per release and host target. Install also activates. Stopped systems expose only state-valid Start, Activate or Deactivate, and Uninstall controls; running systems expose only Stop. Start automatically opens a qualified visual system and starts a nonvisual server without an Open System control.
tradeoffs: Provides the complete user outcome but requires coordinated contract, application, persistence, runtime-session, host, transport, shared-UI, release-rendering, and documentation changes
Preserves audit, rollback, exact-release integrity, workspace isolation, and truthful lifecycle state
Requires explicit handling for partial install-and-activate failure and for a runtime that starts successfully when automatic visual launch fails

consequences: The interface becomes simpler but continues to overstate runtime functionality
Uninstall and deactivate remain aliases or unsupported
A visual system still cannot open after Start
options.label: Existing command facade
options.summary: Move the existing operations into Publish, automatically select identifiers, and keep the current install, activate, and zero-output run semantics.
tradeoffs: Avoids new persistence and runtime-session contracts
Does not launch the created system or provide meaningful Start and Stop behavior

consequences: Uninstall physically removes state and can orphan or erase historical evidence
Failure recovery cannot reliably distinguish stopped, lost, or deleted sessions
Conflicts with the repository's retained immutable release and audited deployment posture
options.label: Ephemeral destructive lifecycle
options.summary: Launch a temporary interface directly from a release and delete deployment and session records when stopped or uninstalled.
tradeoffs: Simple visible lifecycle with fewer retained records
Weakens audit, rollback, reconciliation, recovery, and operational history
Creates destructive deletion and cross-host consistency problems

decisions.question: How should Publish expose install, activation, execution, launch, stop, and uninstall without asking users to manage deployment internals?
decisions.title: Published system lifecycle model

constraints: Immutable releases and archived system history must remain retained and restorable.
Lifecycle filtering belongs in application-owned eligibility, not renderer clients or persistence deletion.
Discovery, preparation, and invocation must all reject missing, archived, cross-workspace, or mismatched owning systems.
Reviewed execution-plan workflows remain governed by their separate plan lifecycle.

abuseCases: An archived system release remains selectable and can be invoked.
A release whose owning system record is missing or belongs to another workspace is treated as active.
A system is archived after discovery but before preparation or invocation.
assets: Deployment, data, and artifact-review action authority
controls: Application handlers derive eligibility from the authoritative workspace-owned system record.
Missing, archived, cross-workspace, and system-id-mismatched records fail closed.
Preparation and invocation re-check lifecycle eligibility instead of trusting a prior summary.
residualRisks: Previously installed deployments remain separate retained operational records and are not deleted by this visibility fix.
securityImpact.summary: The fix changes which workspace-owned immutable releases may cross the Run and Test interaction and execution boundary.
trustBoundaries: System Builder lifecycle repository to application workflow discovery
Prepared release profile to explicit application invocation
Workspace-scoped host composition to API and IPC projections
verification: Focused discovery omission tests for archived and missing systems.
Focused stale lifecycle denial tests for preparation and invocation.
Desktop and server host-composition checks plus repository gates.

sources.title: Predecessor roadmap

discovery.summary: Release-backed workflow handlers currently query immutable releases without joining their owning System Builder lifecycle record. Archived records retain immutable releases by design, so those releases remain discoverable until application-owned workflow eligibility checks active ownership.

feedback.nextAction: Revise the pending increment so authoritative active-source eligibility also projects the same human-recognizable system and build identity used by Publish.
feedback.summary: Publish identifies an approved source by active system name and build version, while Run & Test lists opaque release identifiers alongside releases retained for archived systems. Local metadata confirms one active published release and two archived-system releases, making the active build difficult to identify even though both surfaces share one repository.

feedback.nextAction: Approve a retained deployment and runtime-session lifecycle model, then revise the pending roadmap to consolidate Publish and remove the standalone Run & Test experience.
feedback.summary: Replace the identifier-driven Run & Test workflow with state-aware lifecycle controls on each published build in Publish. Users must not enter deployment or run identifiers, dependent actions must appear only when eligible, and starting a qualified visual system must provide a real release-bound interface rather than a bookkeeping-only handoff.

feedback.nextAction: Replace the pending lifecycle proposal with the clarified intent-driven state model and obtain explicit approval.
feedback.summary: The consolidated Publish lifecycle must expose only state-valid intent controls. Install also activates. A stopped installed system may be started, deactivated when active, activated when inactive, or uninstalled. Starting a visual system opens its release-bound interface automatically, while starting a server starts it without an Open System control. A running system exposes only Stop.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every supported active published build is discoverable in Run & Test with a deterministic system-name and build-version label that maps to its exact immutable release.
Release-backed Run & Test profiles omit releases whose owning system is archived, deleted, cross-workspace, or mismatched while retaining their immutable history.
Preparation and invocation re-read active owning-system state and fail closed when lifecycle eligibility changes after discovery.
Desktop and server compose the same authoritative source catalog, and shared UI tests prove published-source labels remain recognizable without renderer-owned authority.
Workspace isolation, exact release integrity, lifecycle authority, fail-closed denial, secure rollback, retained immutable history, and residual deployment-record risk are documented and evidenced.
Focused catalog, handler, host, and UI tests pass before applicable documentation, architecture, build, and full repository gates run once for the completed increment.

deliverables: Active lifecycle checks in every release-backed workflow handler
Recognizable Run & Test source labels correlated to Publish system and build versions
Archived, deleted, mismatched, stale-lifecycle, identity-correlation, and UI regression tests
Updated workflow architecture, context guidance, and temporary report
excluded: Deleting immutable releases, builds, revisions, deployments, runs, or audit records
Changing archive and restore semantics in Manage
Renderer-only filtering or renderer-owned release identity
Changing release digests or republishing existing releases
increments.objective: Make Run & Test expose supported workflows only for active published systems and label each exact release with the same recognizable system and build identity shown in Publish.
increments.rollback: Remove the catalog-backed release workflow registrations so Run & Test fails closed while immutable releases, builds, system records, deployments, runs, and audit history remain unchanged.
increments.title: Authoritative published-source catalog
verification: Run focused source-catalog tests that correlate active Publish build summaries to exact Run & Test release sources and exclude archived, deleted, cross-workspace, and mismatched owners.
Run focused records, review, and deployment handler tests for discovery plus post-discovery lifecycle denial.
Run focused desktop/server composition and shared UI interaction tests for recognizable labels and capability-specific workflows.
After the complete increment, run documentation, architecture, server and thin-client builds, and npm test once.

workPackages.outcome: Application-owned discovery joins active System Builder records, completed builds, and immutable releases into one workspace-scoped exact-source catalog with deterministic system and build labels.
